haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes. The Inventory sweeper, running every minute, marks lapsed holds EXPIRED and puts the stock back on sale. A later commit fails, so the order becomes a late success and is refunded.
haiku-low.q2: Before the customer is charged. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, short items are returned, the order is REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, and no payment is requested.
haiku-low.q3: The charge is keyed by order id and stored as one PENDING row unique on order id. A retry with the same key finds the existing charge and returns it, so the provider does not charge twice.
haiku-low.q4: The order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is emailed, and Payment refunds the full amount. The refund is retried until the provider confirms it.
haiku-low.q5: After ChargeSucceeded and a successful Inventory commit, when Order publishes OrderConfirmed. Cart removes only the confirmed lines. If checkout fails, the cart is unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service moves the checkout through its statuses (PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED and so on). Order stores the status with the order.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment records it and writes an outbox row, which sends ChargeSucceeded or ChargeDeclined through the message broker to Order. A reconcile timer can query the provider if no webhook arrives.
haiku-low.q8: The webhook receiver checks whether the provider event id was already processed and returns 200 with no change if so. Consumers also check current state before acting.
haiku-low.q9: ChargeDeclined from the broker triggers it. Order sets CANCELLED_DECLINED and asks Inventory to release the hold at once, putting the stock back on sale.
haiku-low.q10: Inventory commits only if the reservation is still HELD and expires_at is in the future. If so, the order is fulfilled. If not, the commit fails and Order refunds the payment.
haiku-low.q11: The refund row stays open, and Payment retries with backoff until the provider confirms. Ops are alerted after N tries. The pending refund is tracked in Payment's refund row.
haiku-low.q12: Successful commit of the order's stock, which Order confirms by publishing OrderConfirmed. The Cart service then removes the confirmed lines only.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes (HELD, expires_at = now + 10 min). If not committed in time, the sweeper (runs every minute) marks it EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, short items are returned, order becomes REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK, no payment is requested, and Cart shows the short items.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) plus a charge row unique on order id. A retry finds the existing charge and returns it, and the provider does not charge twice.
sonnet.q4: Order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is emailed, and Payment refunds the full amount (retried until it succeeds).
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied (confirmed lines removed) after the order is CONFIRMED, on the OrderConfirmed event. On any failure (short stock, decline, late success) the cart stays unchanged and the customer may retry.
sonnet.q6: Events through the message broker (with outbox) and direct requests move steps; Order orchestrates. The record of progress is the Order service's order status (PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, etc.).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which records it and writes an outbox row. The outbox sends ChargeSucceeded or ChargeDeclined via the message broker to Order, which finishes the order. If no webhook arrives, the reconcile timer queries the provider.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores processed provider event ids. A duplicate event id gets a 200 with no change. Also the charge only moves forward, and consumers check current state before acting.
sonnet.q9: The ChargeDeclined event from the broker triggers Order to set CANCELLED_DECLINED and ask Inventory to release the hold at once. Stock goes back on sale. Release is idempotent.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to commit. Inventory checks in one transaction whether the reservation is still HELD and expires_at is in the future. If yes, the stock is sold and the order is confirmed. If no, the order is CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK and fully refunded. It does not re-reserve.
sonnet.q11: The refund row stays open (FAILED), and Payment retries with backoff until the provider confirms, alerting ops after N tries. The row is never dropped. It is tracked in the refund row in the Payment service.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event (published by Order after CONFIRMED) triggers Cart to remove the confirmed lines only. Cart service does it.
